Subject: Request: standard per-1M token IO rates + model list for hosted API

Hi Mina,

Quick intro — I’m Sasha (Head of Product at SlateCare). We’re evaluating hosted providers for chat-driven patient intake and triage. Before we jump into an evaluation call, could you send your standard per-1M token rates split by input vs output (if you price that way) and a simple list of hosted models you support today (and which are recommended for high-accuracy conversational tasks)?

To give a sense of scale: expected pilot ~3M tokens/mo (mostly chat: ~1.2k input average, 120–350 token outputs) with potential to ramp to ~18–25M tokens/mo over 12 months. We care about accuracy first, then latency. Also curious if there are any volume discounts or pilot pricing available.

If you could include an attachment-friendly one-page summary or a link to your rate sheet, that’d be great.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call after you send numbers.

Best,
Sasha Patel
Head of Product | SlateCare
S: @sasha_p

Hi Sasha — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the context — that scale is in the sweet spot for a hosted pilot. I’ve looped in Ben (solutions) for model recommendations and Laura (CS) for any contractual/discount guidance.

Attached is a short summary (one-pager) with baseline per-1M rates and the current hosted model roster. Quick highlights below so you can skim:
• Baseline hosted IO pricing (per 1M tokens):
  - Small/Open models (low-cost): input $0.40 / 1M, output $0.80 / 1M
  - Mid-tier (general purpose): input $0.75 / 1M, output $1.50 / 1M
  - High-accuracy / long-context: input $1.60 / 1M, output $3.20 / 1M

• Models currently available on Hosted API: Compact-1, Gen-1, Redwood-xt-medium, Redwood-xt-large (high-accuracy), Llama2-Chat-70B (quantized variants), and a curated set of faster, lower-cost variants.

Notes:
- We price IO separately for transparency (some customers prefer a single per-token blended rate; we can provide that view if helpful).
- Pilot discounts: we typically offer a one-time pilot credit and a ramp discount for commitments that scale past ~10M tokens/mo. Exact numbers depend on contract length and MRC.

Ben — any model/latency tips for their workload? Laura — we’ll want to call out the typical pilot discount band and any required PO/invoice cadence.

Next steps: I can book a 30-minute call early next week to walk through the one-pager and the SE’s recommendations. What’s your availability?

— Mina

Thanks Mina — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications before we jump on a call:
1) For the high-accuracy tier (Redwood-xt-large): can you share a rough inference latency expectation (p95) for chat-style requests at our pilot scale (3M tokens/mo) and at the ramped scale (20M tokens/mo)? We need to ensure sub-800ms generative tail for patient-facing UI.
2) Do you have published guidance on token accounting for multipart form inputs (we’ll be sending structured JSON with metadata + user text)?
3) On pricing — is the pilot credit a dollar amount or an IO discount? And is the ramp discount applied after crossing a monthly threshold or as an up-front committed discount?

Also, open to mid-tier models if latency improves and accuracy stays acceptable.

— Sasha
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: standard per-1M token IO rates + model list for hosted API

Hi Sasha — Ben on solutions here. Quick answers and a recommended path: 

Latency (p95) estimates on Hosted (multi-tenant optimized runtime):
• Pilot (~3M tokens/mo): Redwood-xt-large ~420–650ms p95 for typical chat sequences (subject to prompt length). Mid-tier models are ~220–350ms p95.
• Ramped (~20M tokens/mo): baseline p95s are similar if requests are well-distributed; if traffic spikes, we recommend configuring burst capacity or reserving a dedicated pool (Dedicated) — hosted can maintain SLOs but dedicated guarantees are stronger.

Token accounting: structured JSON metadata + user text is charged on final serialized tokenization (we count input tokens after canonical serialization). We can share a small helper snippet to estimate tokens for your payloads.

Pricing mechanics: pilot credit is a dollar-denominated credit applied to the first invoice; ramp discounts are available as either (a) a post-threshold volume discount that kicks in after monthly usage crosses the agreed threshold, or (b) an upfront committed discount applied as a reduced per-1M rate in the contract. We typically see customers prefer committed discounts for predictability.

Recommendation: Start pilot on Redwood-xt-large for accuracy, instrument with token sampling and latency tracing, then evaluate switching some routes to a mid-tier model for cost-sensitive flows. I’m attaching a short rate summary and a sample token-counting script.

If useful, we can open a temporary burst reservation for the pilot week to tighten tail latency while you validate UX.

— Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
